industry: Process Control & Yield Management / Inspection & Metrology
thesis: KLA Corporation is the dominant global supplier of semiconductor process control and yield management equipment — inspection, metrology, and data analytics tools that are essential for manufacturing defect-free chips at every node. FY2026 revenue grew 12% to $13.6B with Q4 revenue of $3.66B (+15.2% YoY) and GAAP EPS of $1.04. Advanced packaging process control revenues are expected to reach ~$1.1B in calendar 2026 as AI accelerator and HBM packaging complexity drives rising inspection intensity. At ~48x trailing P/E and ~$252B market cap, the stock is moderately valued for a high-quality WFE company with 60%+ gross margins and best-in-class capital returns ($4.9B cash). BUY — process control is the least cyclical WFE segment and KLA is the monopoly-like leader.

drivers: Advanced packaging inspection revenue reaches $1.1B+ as HBM and chiplet packaging complexity grows
Rising process control intensity at GAA and EUV nodes increases KLA's content per wafer
FY2027 revenue accelerates as AI-driven WFE spending continues and China remains elevated
Capital return program (dividends + buybacks) provides downside protection and shareholder value

base_case.assumptions: FY2027 revenue grows 10–15% to ~$15–16B as process control spending tracks broader WFE expansion. Gross margins hold above 60%. EPS reaches ~$4.20–4.60. Market applies a 50–55x P/E for the quality premium, keeping the stock near current levels.

risks: WFE cyclical correction compresses process control spending and multiples
China export controls escalate, restricting KLA's access to Chinese fabs
Advanced packaging process control growth disappoints as chiplet adoption slows
Broad semiconductor de-rating event driven by AI capex concerns

catalysts.event: Q4 FY2026 results — revenue $3.66B (+15.2%), advanced packaging process control update
Q1 FY2027 earnings (expected late October) — FY2027 demand outlook
Advanced packaging and EUV inspection tool adoption at leading-edge fabs

key_risks: WFE cyclicality: even process control (the least cyclical segment) can see 10–15% revenue declines in downturns
China exposure: tightening export controls could restrict sales to Chinese semiconductor fabs
Rich valuation at ~48x P/E; any growth deceleration could trigger multiple compression
Customer concentration: TSMC, Samsung, Intel/IFS represent the bulk of capex
Stock fell sharply after Q4 beat (~21% from 52-week high of $307 to ~$193), signaling elevated sentiment risk
